## Observed fixture behavior
Persistent WAL SQLite with scoped records, guarded BEGIN IMMEDIATE, atomic state/receipt writes, one-time migration of duplicate legacy IDs, refusal of overlapping historically spent IDs, exact-unit debit, receipt replay, independent worker connections, failure before commit and lost response after commit. Synthetic trusted acquisition occurrence survives consumption and restore, and separate scopes cannot mutate each other. Candidate explicit backup restores prior material snapshot, keeps receipt history, increments epoch/revision, and rejects old-epoch debit. Projection classification rejects same-revision differing payload, stale revision, stale epoch and wrong scope. Test data only; no actual authorization, real catalog, capacity, production transaction guarantee, runtime migration or full Character Vault restore. Worker connections test competing requests, not stress testing or process crash; failure injected, not actual power loss. Same-revision comparison uses serialized object order, not canonical equivalence. Projection does not install new restore epoch, and backup restore lacks replay acknowledgement; it is not a full snapshot adapter. Restoring post-backup acquisitions requires explicit approved policy and discovery redelivery, not fixture's simplified behavior. No real data touched.
